This module introduces no new regulation, standard, or framework, and no new source was
fetched for it. Its entire job is crosswalking ITIL (Information Technology Infrastructure
Library) vocabulary — the learner's own professional background, never itself cited to a
specific AXELOS/PeopleCert publication anywhere in this curriculum — onto two mechanics
`quality-system-essentials` already built and locked. The first two links below are the direct
inputs this module maps against; read either one for the actual process mechanics and
citations, which this module deliberately doesn't redevelop.

- **[Change control for regulated
  systems](../../quality-system-essentials/change-control-for-regulated-systems/index.qmd)** —
  the five-stage process (change request, impact and risk assessment, approval, implementation,
  verification) this module's first crosswalk maps ITIL's change enablement practice onto,
  including the regulatory grounding (21 CFR 606.100(b)) and the AABB (Association for the
  Advancement of Blood & Biotherapies) Process Control QSE (Quality System Essential) behind it.
  Read it for the actual citation decoder, verbatim regulatory text, and the full stage-by-stage
  mechanics this lesson references by name but doesn't re-quote.

- **[CAPA: root cause to effectiveness
  check](../../quality-system-essentials/capa-root-cause-to-effectiveness/index.qmd)** — the
  four-stage CAPA (corrective and preventive action) structure (root cause analysis, corrective
  action, preventive action, effectiveness check) this module's second crosswalk maps ITIL's
  problem management practice onto, including the regulatory grounding (21 CFR 606.100(c) and
  606.171(f)) and the AABB Process Improvement QSE behind it. Read it for the actual root-cause
  technique (5 Whys), the four required pieces of a real effectiveness check, and the three
  possible closure outcomes (close, extend, reopen) this lesson references but doesn't
  redevelop.

- **[Problem management features in Jira Service Management](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B6zA8MkJ7Ew)**
  (Atlassian, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. A vendor's tool
  walkthrough of problem records, useful for seeing ITIL's problem-management side of the second
  crosswalk in practice. It is a product demo, not blood- or CAPA-specific. Verified embeddable via
  YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Change enablement in ITIL 4 — AWS Well-Architected, Change Enablement in the
  Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/change-enablement-in-the-cloud/change-enablement-in-itil4.html)**
  — a cloud provider's plain-language summary of the ITIL 4 change enablement practice (assessing
  risk, authorizing, scheduling). Read it for the ITIL side of crosswalk 1 stated by someone other
  than this lesson. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Change Enablement – Change Management in ITIL 4 (itsm.tools)](https://itsm.tools/change-enablement/)**
  — an industry explainer on what shifted from ITIL v3's change management to ITIL 4's change
  enablement and what that looks like day to day, including the role of the change authority. Good
  background for the CAB-versus-required-approver contrast. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Atlassian: What is change management in ITSM?](https://www.atlassian.com/itsm/change-management)**
  — an industry explainer on change types and approval flows in IT service management. Read it to
  see how an ordinary IT shop defines "standard" versus "normal" changes, the exact label this
  lesson's systems administrator reached for. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Atlassian: Problem Management in ITIL](https://www.atlassian.com/itsm/problem-management)**
  — an industry explainer on the problem-management process, root cause identification, and best
  practices. Read it for the ITIL view of known errors and workarounds before comparing it with
  CAPA's stricter closure standard. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Splunk: IT/ITIL Problem Management](https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/learn/problem-management.html)**
  — a second industry explainer on problem management, incident versus problem, and the known
  error database. Useful as an independent cross-check on the vocabulary used in crosswalk 2.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-128: Guide for Security-Focused Configuration Management of Information
  Systems](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/128/upd1/final)** — a U.S. government publication on
  managing and controlling configuration changes to information systems with security in mind.
  Not blood-specific and not part of this lesson's crosswalk; read it if you want a public,
  government-authored view of change control for IT systems. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about change enablement, problem management and blameless learning.

- **[DORA: Streamlining change approval](https://dora.dev/capabilities/streamlining-change-approval/)** (DORA / Google Cloud research program) — research-backed argument for lightweight, peer-reviewed change approval over heavy committees. A useful counterpoint when you design how much review a change really needs. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Google SRE: Blameless Postmortem for System Resilience](https://sre.google/sre-book/postmortem-culture/)** (Google SRE book) — the classic chapter on learning from failures without blaming people. Good background for the problem-management and root-cause side of this lesson. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[How to run a blameless postmortem](https://www.atlassian.com/incident-management/postmortem/blameless)** (Atlassian, vendor content) — a practical, step-by-step guide to running the review meeting and writing it up. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[What Is a CAB? Change Advisory Board Explained](https://www.atlassian.com/itsm/change-management/change-advisory-board)** (Atlassian, vendor content) — plain-English overview of what a change advisory board does and who sits on it. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[CISSP Domain 7 Review / Mind Map (4 of 6) | Patching & Change Management](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xX4U6Lz82Bk)** (Destination Certification) — a visual CISSP review of change and patch management; supports CISSP Domain 7 (Security Operations). Verified via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
